Let \(\chi:\mathbb F_p^\times\to\{1,i,-1,-i\}\) be the quartic character with \(\chi(g)=i\), extended by \(\chi(0)=0\). Put
\[
\varepsilon=\chi(4)=\left(\frac2p\right)=(-1)^{b/2},
\]
where \(b\) is even since \(p=a^2+b^2\) and \(a\) is odd.

For the diagonal quartic
\[
X^4+Y^4=gZ^4,
\]
the primitive character pairs are
\[
(u,v)\in\{1,2,3\}^2,\qquad u+v\not\equiv0\pmod4.
\]
The corresponding Frobenius eigenvalues are
\[
-\chi^{u+v}(g)J(\chi^u,\chi^v),
\]
where
\[
J(\alpha,\beta)=\sum_{x\in\mathbb F_p}\alpha(x)\beta(1-x).
\]

The quartic Jacobi sum determined by the condition \(br\equiv a\pmod p\) is
\[
J(\chi,\chi)=-a+bi.
\]
Also
\[
J(\chi,\chi^2)=\chi(4)J(\chi,\chi)=\varepsilon(-a+bi),
\]
using the substitution \(x=4t(1-t)\), since the number of \(t\) with \(4t(1-t)=x\) is \(1+\chi^2(1-x)\). Taking conjugates gives the remaining sums.

Thus the six values \(\chi^{u+v}(g)J(\chi^u,\chi^v)\) are
\[
a\pm bi,\qquad \varepsilon(b\pm ai),\qquad \varepsilon(b\pm ai),
\]
so the Frobenius eigenvalues are their negatives. Therefore
\[
L_{C_g}(T)
=(1+2aT+pT^2)(1+2\varepsilon bT+pT^2)^2.
\]

Hence
\[
\boxed{L_{C_g}(T)=\bigl(1+2aT+pT^2\bigr)\bigl(1+2(-1)^{b/2}bT+pT^2\bigr)^2.}
\]
